items.stem: You drop a 24fps clip into a 29.97fps sequence and playback stutters. What is the MOST appropriate first action?

options.text: Match the sequence settings (or interpret) to the dominant footage, then re-add clips
options.rationale: Correct: aligning sequence framerate to the footage avoids conform/stutter issues.
Playback resolution is a preview aid; it does not fix a framerate conform mismatch.
Re-importing does not change how the clip conforms to the sequence framerate.

options.text: Convert the project to a new colour space
options.rationale: Colour space is unrelated to framerate stutter.

items.explanation: Correct: aligning sequence framerate to the footage avoids conform/stutter issues.

items.stem: Which edit type pushes all downstream clips later on the timeline to make room for the new clip?

options.rationale: Correct: an insert edit ripples downstream clips to accommodate the inserted clip.
Overwrite replaces existing frames and does not shift downstream clips.
Lift removes a clip leaving a gap; it does not add a clip.
Extract removes a clip and ripples the gap closed; it does not insert.

items.explanation: Correct: an insert edit ripples downstream clips to accommodate the inserted clip.

items.stem: Which TWO are appropriate when preparing a final export for web delivery?

options.text: Choose a delivery preset matching the target platform's codec and resolution
options.rationale: Correct: platform-matched presets ensure compatible codec/resolution.

options.text: Set a reasonable bitrate for the target file-size and quality
options.rationale: Correct: bitrate drives the quality/size trade-off for web.

options.text: Always export uncompressed to guarantee quality
options.rationale: Uncompressed files are impractically large and unnecessary for web delivery.

options.text: Disable audio to reduce file size
options.rationale: Dropping audio changes the deliverable and is not a standard web optimisation.

items.explanation: Correct: platform-matched presets ensure compatible codec/resolution.
